label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: Desks with legs and shelves, a freestanding chalkboard, ceiling fans, floor, walls and ceiling are recognizable beyond featureless cubes.

The furniture forms a widely spaced uniform grid instead of the reference's denser, irregular rows. Repeated narrow wall panels do not reproduce the varied openings, and the stage occupies too little of the far wall.
Bags reach approximately desktop height, desks are too small relative to the room and openings, and the stage and board are undersized relative to room width.

The cream/yellow walls and green/burgundy stage retain palette cues, but pale tan furniture replaces dark wood and uniform illumination loses the strong side daylight and dark stage recess. These differences exceed matte simplification.

Box.123 is a finite mesh with 8 vertices, 6 polygons and dimensions 1.55 × 0.64 × 0.10, bound to SceneActSurface_6. Rod has 64 vertices, 34 polygons and nonzero depth. The bound material has a Principled BSDF connected to Material Output.

The enclosed classroom, repeated wooden desks, overhead fans, yellow lower walls and green-framed burgundy stage with chalkboard clearly evoke the supplied classroom despite substantial simplification.

dimension_scores.evidence: Distinctive classroom and stage cues survive, but furniture density, openings and architectural detail differ substantially.
Desks have coherent supporting legs, books rest on tops and fans have downrods. Wall openings and board support remain schematic.
Major accent colors correspond, but light furniture, rigid box-shaped bags and flat curtains lose important silhouettes and tonal relationships.
Identical sharp-edged desks, blank picture frames, slab curtains and block bags create a crude model appearance. Delivery noise further reduces clarity.
Desks face the far teaching area and openings repeat along both sides, but uniform large gaps and reduced stage breadth alter the reference's spatial organization.
Furniture is small within the enclosure, bags are unusually tall beside desks, and the teaching area is too narrow.
Soft shadows establish volume, but washed-out wood and broadly even light poorly reproduce side illumination, material differentiation and the dark stage.
Repeated desks, fans, bags, books and chalkboard are present. Seating, front chairs, cabinets, ceiling beams and tube fixtures are absent or insufficiently represented.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
